s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional basis of NITI Aayog?
o: It was created by an Act of Parliament
It was created by a constitutional amendment
It was created by a Presidential Ordinance
It was created by a Union Cabinet resolution
x: NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body created by a Union Cabinet resolution.
tq: Identify the exact legal instrument instead of assuming that a national institution must be statutory.
sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
2. Its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister.
3. The resolution fixes the number of full-time members at five.
4. Up to two part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson, appoints the Vice-Chairperson, and may nominate up to two part-time members from universities and research bodies. The resolution does not prescribe a fixed number of full-time members.
tq: Test the fixed-number trap by separating provisions that are flexible from those expressly specified.
sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

s: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ex officio members — Up to four Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Part-time members — Permanent representatives of all State Governments
Chief Executive Officer — Elected by the Governing Council
Special invitees — Nominated by the Vice-Chairperson alone
x: NITI Aayog may have up to four ex officio Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister. Its CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister, and special invitees are also nominated by the Prime Minister.
tq: Match each component with the authority responsible for its inclusion or appointment.
sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

s: Ashok Kumar Lahiri assumed the office of Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog on which date?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri, formerly Chief Economic Adviser, was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog on 25 April 2026.
tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the dates of NITI Aayog’s formation and Governing Council meetings.
sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

s: In the planning process followed by the Planning Commission, plans were placed before which sequence of institutions?
x: Plans prepared through the Planning Commission went to the National Development Council, then the Cabinet and thereafter Parliament.
tq: Use the institutional sequence and eliminate bodies not involved in plan approval.
sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Announcement of the abolition of the Planning Commission
B. Formation of NITI Aayog
C. Establishment of the Planning Commission
D. Appointment of Ashok Kumar Lahiri as Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog
x: The Planning Commission was established in March 1950, its abolition was announced on 15 August 2014, NITI Aayog came into existence on 1 January 2015, and Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed on 25 April 2026.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 2014 and 2015 events between them.
sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

s: The abolition of the Planning Commission was announced by which Prime Minister on 15 August 2014?
x: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the abolition of the Planning Commission on 15 August 2014; it was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.
tq: Apply the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap to distinguish the announcing Prime Minister from earlier Prime Ministers.
sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

s: Which approach is most closely associated with the federalism model of NITI Aayog?
o: Judicial federalism controlled by the Supreme Court
Centralised federalism based exclusively on Union directives
Fiscal federalism limited to tax devolution
Cooperative federalism with a bottom-up approach
x: NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism and follows a bottom-up approach. Its State rankings also provide an element of competitive federalism.
tq: Separate the principal approach from related but narrower forms of federalism.
sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated area of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Conducting constitutional litigation for State Governments
x: The four stated areas are knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation. Constitutional litigation is not included among them.
tq: Find the option that does not belong to the official functional group.
sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

s: NITI Aayog is described as the government’s think tank and policy dynamo primarily because it performs which role?
o: It replaces Parliament in making laws
It directly collects all taxes for the Union
It provides policy advice, promotes innovation and supports transformational change
It exercises judicial review over State policies
x: NITI Aayog functions as a policy think tank by providing policy inputs, promoting knowledge and innovation, supporting States and pursuing transformational change.
tq: Infer the institution’s practical role from its advisory and policy-development functions.
sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

s: Which body of NITI Aayog tracks the performance of Union ministries?
x: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office, or DMEO, tracks the performance of ministries.
tq: Match the monitoring function with the specialised evaluation office rather than with a federal-engagement hub.
sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the Governing Council of NITI Aayog:
1. It includes the Prime Minister.
2. It includes the Chief Ministers of all States.
3. It includes the Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories without legislatures.
4. It includes only elected representatives and excludes special invitees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Governing Council includes the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, Lieutenant Governors of other Union Territories, ex officio members, the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members and special invitees. Statement 4 is false.
tq: Test composition by identifying the excluded category hidden behind the word ‘only’.
sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

s: The Chief Ministers of which Union Territories are members of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry
Delhi, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
x: The Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures: Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry.
tq: Use the legislature-based classification to distinguish Union Territories represented by Chief Ministers.
sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are primarily constituted for:
o: Permanent supervision of every State’s finances
Specific regional issues for a fixed period
x: Regional Councils are formed to address specific regional issues and operate for a fixed period. They are chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee and include the Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of the region.
tq: Identify the temporary, issue-specific body rather than attributing permanent constitutional functions to it.
sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

s: Who may chair a Regional Council constituted by NITI Aayog?
o: The Chief Minister of the largest State in the region
The Prime Minister or his nominee
x: A Regional Council is chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee; Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of the concerned region are included in it.
tq: Apply the authority-power test to identify who can chair the body.
sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

s: SETUs, supported by NITI Aayog under the State Support Mission, are intended to help States prepare:
x: NITI Aayog assists States in setting up State Economic and Transformation Units, or SETUs, to prepare State Vision@2047 plans.

sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

Export Preparedness Index — States’ export readiness

It measures e-mobility across States and its second edition used 16 indicators.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the difference between the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog regarding financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog allocates plan funds, whereas the Planning Commission had only advisory powers.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds, whereas NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and works with the Finance Ministry.
Both allocate plan funds directly to ministries and States.
Neither institution has any relationship with the allocation of public funds.

tq: Compare the institutional power rather than the broad policy objectives.
sec: NITI vs Planning Commission - fund allocation, approach

s:
Which of the following correctly contrasts the approaches of the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
1. The Planning Commission followed a top-down approach.
2. NITI Aayog follows bottom-up planning.
3. NITI Aayog is associated with cooperative federalism.
